Canterbury is a thriving area with strong demand for reliable full bathroom installation and fitting services. Local properties range from period Victorian and Edwardian homes through to modern new-build developments, each presenting different plumbing requirements and challenges.

Our Gas Safe registered engineers serve all areas of Canterbury and the surrounding Kent region. Whether you're in the town centre or the surrounding residential areas, we provide prompt, professional bathroom installation services with transparent pricing and no hidden call-out charges.

With years of experience working across Kent, our engineers understand the specific plumbing challenges faced by local homeowners. From the older pipe infrastructure common in period properties to the modern systems found in newer developments, our team has the expertise to handle any full bathroom installation and fitting requirement.

We cover all postcodes across Canterbury with same-day availability for urgent work. All our engineers are fully qualified, insured, and committed to leaving your property clean and tidy after every job.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a new bathroom?
faqs.a: In most cases, no. Replacing like-for-like or fitting a new bathroom within existing walls does not require planning permission. Moving soil stacks or creating a new bathroom in unconverted space may require Building Regulations approval.

faqs.q: Can you move the toilet and bath to different positions?
faqs.a: Yes, but it depends on the soil pipe route and floor structure. Moving a toilet more than a metre from the existing soil stack requires a new soil pipe connection and increases cost significantly.

faqs.q: How much does a bathroom installation cost?
faqs.a: Labour for a full bathroom installation typically ranges from £2,500 to £5,000 depending on complexity. Suite and tile costs are separate. A complete bathroom renovation including all materials typically costs £4,000 to £10,000+.

faqs.q: Should I supply my own bathroom suite or let the plumber supply it?
faqs.a: You can do either. Supplying your own suite gives you more choice and control over the brand and style. Your installer may offer trade discounts worth 15-30% off RRP if they supply.

localParagraph: Canterbury, Kent, presents a varied landscape for bathroom installation, with properties ranging from Victorian terraces near the city centre to post-war semis in areas such as Wincheap and Sturry Road, and newer builds on the outskirts toward Thanington and Herne Bay Road. This mix of housing eras means that plumbers and bathroom fitters must be well-versed in adapting modern installations to older pipework configurations, where cast iron waste pipes and outdated soil stacks are still commonly encountered. Canterbury also sits within a zone of mixed water hardness, drawing from both chalk aquifers and softer surface water sources, which can influence the choice of fixtures, boiler compatibility, and long-term maintenance requirements — hard water areas in particular benefit from scale-reducing devices fitted during installation. Homeowners across the city, whether renovating a period property close to the cathedral quarter or updating a bathroom in a modern estate development, would do well to engage a qualified installer familiar with these local conditions, ensuring both compliance with current building regulations and a result that performs reliably for years to come.
whatItInvolves: A full bathroom installation covers everything from stripping out the existing suite to fitting the new one — including all pipework, waste connections, tiling preparation, flooring, and electrical work for lighting and extraction. A quality bathroom installation transforms one of the most-used rooms in your home and typically adds 3-5% to your property value.
process: The process starts with a detailed survey to assess existing pipework, drainage routes, and structural considerations. Day 1-2: strip out and prep. Day 3-4: first fix plumbing and any structural work. Day 5-7: suite installation, tiling, and second fix. Day 8-10: finishing, sealant, and final inspection. You'll be without a working bathroom for 5-10 days depending on complexity — we'll agree a realistic timeline upfront.
whatToExpect: Expect a detailed written quote covering labour, waste disposal, and any structural work. Suite and tiles are usually supplied separately by you or sourced through us. All plumbing work is carried out to Water Regulations standards. A bathroom installation is a major investment — ask to see previous work and Gas Safe registration before committing to any installer.
